breaks.expected: Native validation must be at least as strict as the JS read-back parser (reject with invalid_receipt, write nothing) or the wrapper must refuse the receipt before calling native; a natively committed wallet must never be unreadable through the typed bridge. VERIFIED on Linux JSONSerialization (swift-6.0.3); Apple's JSONSerialization documents that input 'may or may not have a BOM' (INFERRED for iOS, rerun the Swift test on the Mac runner to confirm).
breaks.observed: OfflineWallet.replace(...receipts:[payloadJson:"\u{FEFF}{...}"]) returns a revision-1 snapshot and writes 264 bytes to wallet.v1.<owner> (OfflineWalletShape.isJsonObject uses JSONSerialization, which tolerates a BOM). TS replaceOfflineWallet rejects with failure 'bridge_contract' (parseSnapshot -> isJsonObjectText -> JSON.parse throws) AFTER native.replaceWallet resolved; the fake native shows walletRevision 1. Every later loadOfflineWallet(owner) rejects bridge_contract, discardCorruptOfflineWallet rejects not_corrupt (native verifies fine), and clear needs the revision the caller never received.
breaks.repro: Swift (Linux surrogate of native/vision-core): cd ~/surrogate && swift test --filter OfflineWalletAttackTests/testReplaceRejectsReceiptPayloadWithByteOrderMarkThatJsCannotParse ; Jest: cd apps/mobile && npx jest __tests__/offlineWalletNativeAttack.test.ts -t 'refuses a receipt payload JS cannot parse back'
breaks.title: Native accepts a receipt payload the JS bridge cannot parse (UTF-8 BOM) -> replace commits the wallet natively but rejects bridge_contract; owner's wallet then unreadable from JS (load -> bridge_contract, discardCorrupt -> not_corrupt)

breaks.expected: discardCorrupt must throw not_corrupt (or re-read/CAS-verify the key before deleting) and leave wallet/fence intact. Reachability: the shipping bridge uses one OfflineWallet on a serial queue, so this needs a second instance/process — but OfflineWallet.swift's own header documents exactly that multi-instance/multi-process concurrency as a supported case.
breaks.observed: readState reads key -> fence -> wallet as three non-atomic store reads. Instance B completes the owner's first replace (key+fence+wallet, receipt 'receipt-unsent') between A's key read (nil) and A's fence read. A's discardCorrupt classifies the state as integrityKeyMissing ('wallet present without its integrity key'), which satisfies isUnreadableState, and deletes wallet.v1.<owner> and fence.v1.<owner>; load afterwards returns nil — the committed receipt is gone with no error.
breaks.title: discardCorrupt racing another OfflineWallet instance's first write for the same owner deletes a healthy wallet and its fence (unsent receipt lost)

breaks.expected: Either nil (pre-write view) or the revision-1 snapshot; a concurrent legitimate write must only ever be observed as wallet-ahead-of-fence, as the doc comment promises for the fence — the same reasoning must cover the key read.
breaks.observed: Same interleaving as above: load throws OfflineWalletError(integrityKeyMissing, 'wallet present without its integrity key'), an outcome the TS wrapper treats as isOfflineWalletUnreadable => callers are steered to discardCorrupt.
breaks.title: load racing another instance's first write is reported as integrity_key_missing (unreadable-state failure) for a healthy owner

breaks.expected: clear must commit the fence to the observed wallet revision (as replace does) so revision 2 is never handed out twice and the older authentic envelope is detected as rollback. Requires a crash in the wallet->fence window plus a later Keychain restore, hence P2.
breaks.observed: Wallet at revision 2, fence left at 1 (process died before commitFence). Relaunched instance: load -> revision 2 (ok), clear(expectedRevision: 2) deletes the wallet and leaves fence=1, next replace(expectedRevision: 0) returns revision 2 (expected 3). Restoring the pre-clear revision-2 envelope then loads as current state (no .tampered), although the doc comment states 'the fence survives clear, so revisions never restart for an owner on this installation'.
breaks.title: clear after a crash between the wallet write and the fence commit does not repair the fence -> the next replace reuses a revision number and the pre-clear authentic envelope replays as current state

breaks.expected: invalid_receipt, nothing written. Must be re-run on the Mac runner: if Apple's JSONSerialization rejects the trailing comma this entry is Linux-surrogate-only and not a shipping break.
breaks.observed: replace returns revision 1 and writes 197 bytes for payloadJson '{"a":1,}'; node JSON.parse of the same text throws.
breaks.title: Trailing-comma JSON receipt payload ('{"a":1,}') accepted natively, rejected by JSON.parse (same bridge-wedge chain as the BOM break) — VERIFIED on Linux swift-6.0.3 JSONSerialization only, Apple parser UNKNOWN

breaks.expected: Design limitation rather than a coding defect: the fence lives in the same Keychain store as the item it fences, so a whole-store restore cannot be detected without an out-of-store monotonic anchor. Reported so the 'anti-rollback' claim in the implementer summary is scoped correctly.
breaks.observed: After revision 2 (grant spent, receipt stored), restoring both wallet.v1.<owner> and fence.v1.<owner> bytes from revision 1 loads as revision 1 with the spent grant present and the receipt gone; no .tampered.
breaks.title: Full-state rollback (wallet AND fence restored from the same earlier point) is indistinguishable from current state — anti-rollback only covers a partial restore

W05-01 round 3 on branch devin/pp/w05-01/impl-r3 (HEAD 1549b6aa, base ca616aa0). Reused the sound r2 commits (15d24887, 5500b8a8, a94db531, b2e54566: bridge module PickleOfflineWallet.swift/.m, podspec + Core symlink wiring, TS wrapper) and rebuilt the core to resolve every r2 adversary finding.

Defects on BASE/r2 (VERIFIED via Linux SwiftPM surrogate + Jest): (1) one device-wide `integrity-key.v1` item — a wrong-length key made every owner's wallet unwritable and discardCorrupt returned .notCorrupt / deleted the intact wallet but kept the bad key (OfflineWallet.swift r2 readVerified/discardCorrupt); (2) no anti-rollback — restoring an older MAC-valid envelope was read as current state; (3) 8 max grants + 64 realistic receipts exceeded the 1 MiB envelope (JSON re-escaping); (4) revision fence was check-then-write — two OfflineWallet instances lost an unsent receipt; (5) stored revision ≥ 2^53 accepted then replace at 2^53-1 produced 2^53 / UInt64.max trapped on `+ 1`; (6–8) TS parseSnapshot did not check owner equality, duplicate/empty ids, counts, payload object-ness, or discard outcome set.

Fix (native/vision-core/Sources/OfflineWallet.swift, commit b1fc989a): per-owner integrity key (`integrity-key.v1.<owner>`), per-owner wallet item and per-owner sealed revision fence (`fence.v1.<owner>`); binary envelope `[version][32-byte HMAC][payload]` with the tag bound to account + version + payload so bytes cannot be moved between owners or between wallet/fence; `OfflineWalletSecureStore` is now compare-and-swap (`write(account:data:ifUnchangedFrom:)`, `delete(account:ifUnchangedFrom:)`) and `KeychainOfflineWalletStore` implements it with `kSecAttrGeneric = SHA-256(item bytes)` as the CAS predicate, so a concurrent writer gets `.revisionConflict` instead of silently overwriting; reads go key → fence → wallet (reverse of write order wallet → fence) so a legitimate in-flight replace is only ever observed as wallet-ahead-of-fence (repaired on the next write), never as a spurious rollback; a wallet revision behind the fence is `.tampered`; `clear` keeps the fence; `discardCorrupt` removes a corrupt key/wallet/fence for that owner only and preserves a verified fence; revisions are bounded to `maxRevision = 2^53-1` on read (`.tampered` above) and on write (`.capacityExceeded` at the ceiling, no overflow); envelope budget raised so `Limits` (8 grants × 16 KiB JWS + 64 receipts × 8 KiB payload) is always storable. TS wrapper (apps/mobile/src/native/offlineWallet.ts) hardened: owner equality, OFFLINE_WALLET_LIMITS counts, non-empty/unique ids, payloadJson must parse to a non-null non-array object, discard resolves only unreadable failures. Shipping bridge (PickleOfflineWallet.swift / Bridge.m) unchanged in r3 — it already constructs `OfflineWallet(store: KeychainOfflineWalletStore())` and is compiled by the pod via the podspec + Sources/Core/OfflineWallet.swift symlink.

Live Keychain compare-and-swap semantics (SecItemUpdate/SecItemDelete with kSecAttrGeneric digest predicate, kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain on iOS) are INFERRED from the Security API: the Mac run's OfflineWalletTests only assert the query dictionaries; no test calls SecItem* against a real keychain. W05-05 (simulator launch/store/kill/restore) is the package that must prove this on device.

discardCorrupt deletes the owner's wallet item whenever the FENCE is unverifiable (OfflineWallet.swift readState 409-411 -> discardCorrupt 297-301), even if the wallet envelope itself verifies — conservative (cannot rule out rollback) and only reachable after server reconciliation per the doc comment, but callers should know a corrupt fence costs the unsent receipts locally.

After discardCorrupt removes a corrupt fence, the owner's revision sequence restarts at 1, so an attacker who can write the app's Keychain could then re-plant an older authentic envelope with revision >= the new fence. Inherent to any fence-deletion path; server reconciliation remains authoritative. Defense-in-depth note only.
